### Setup with Interactive Wizard

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/setup.md

Initializes the configuration and workspace, and then runs the interactive onboarding wizard. This is useful for first-time setup or when guided configuration is needed.

```bash
openclaw setup --wizard
```

--------------------------------

### Install and Run LiteLLM Proxy

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/litellm.md

Install the LiteLLM proxy with the necessary dependencies and start the service. This is part of the manual setup process.

```bash
pip install 'litellm[proxy]'
litellm --model claude-opus-4-6
```

--------------------------------

### Install and Setup Honcho Plugin

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/memory-honcho.md

Install the Honcho plugin and run the setup command to configure API credentials and migrate existing memory. The gateway is then restarted to apply changes.

```bash
openclaw plugins install @honcho-ai/openclaw-honcho
openclaw honcho setup
openclaw gateway --force
```

### Groq Provider Configuration File Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/groq.md

Complete configuration example showing environment variable setup and default model configuration for Groq in OpenClaw.

```json5
{
  env: { GROQ_API_KEY: "gsk_..." },
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      model: { primary: "groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile" },
    },

}
```

### Onboard and install OpenClaw as a daemon service

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/index.md

Run the onboarding wizard and install OpenClaw as a background service. This sets up the Gateway with guided configuration and pairing flows.

```bash
openclaw onboard --install-daemon
```

--------------------------------

### Manual Docker setup flow

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/docker.md

Alternative to the setup script: build image, run onboarding and config setup through openclaw-gateway directly, then start the gateway. Run from repo root; include docker-compose.extra.yml if OPENCLAW_EXTRA_MOUNTS or OPENCLAW_HOME_VOLUME are enabled.

```bash
docker build -t openclaw:local -f Dockerfile .
docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint node openclaw-gateway \
  dist/index.js onboard --mode local --no-install-daemon
docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint node openclaw-gateway \
  dist/index.js config set --batch-json '[{"path":"gateway.mode","value":"local"},{"path":"gateway.bind","value":"lan"},{"path":"gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins","value":["http://localhost:18789","http://127.0.0.1:18789"]}]'
docker compose up -d openclaw-gateway
```

--------------------------------

### Install and Run Convex Dev Server

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/qa/convex-credential-broker/README.md

Installs project dependencies and starts the local Convex development server. Ensure you are in the `qa/convex-credential-broker` directory.

```bash
cd qa/convex-credential-broker
npm install
npx convex dev
```

### Manual git clone and build setup


--------------------------------

### Clone and install OpenClaw from source with pnpm

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/README.md

Initial setup for development: clone the repository, install dependencies using pnpm (required for workspace support), and run setup. The repository is a pnpm workspace where bundled plugins load from extensions/ during development.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
cd openclaw

pnpm install

# First run only (or after resetting local OpenClaw config/workspace)
pnpm openclaw setup

# Optional: prebuild Control UI before first startup
pnpm ui:build

# Dev loop (auto-reload on source/config changes)
pnpm gateway:watch
```

Initiates the command-line interface onboarding process. Use this for server, headless, or script-based setups.

```bash
openclaw onboard
```

--------------------------------

### Start an OpenClaw Node Host Service (Bash)

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/nodes/index.md

Install and manage an OpenClaw node as a background service. The `install` command sets up the node, while `start` and `restart` control its execution.

```bash
openclaw node install --host <gateway-host> --port 18789 --display-name "Build Node"
openclaw node start
openclaw node restart
```

### Rescue Bot Quickstart

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/multiple-gateways.md

Installs a rescue Gateway with a separate profile and port. Ensure your main bot is already running.

```bash
# Rescue bot (separate Telegram bot, separate profile, port 19789)
openclaw --profile rescue onboard
openclaw --profile rescue gateway install --port 19789
```

### Setup Local PostgreSQL on Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/open-prose/skills/prose/state/postgres.md

Steps to install and manage PostgreSQL on Debian/Ubuntu systems. This involves using apt to install the package, starting the service, creating a database, and setting the connection URL in the .prose/.env file.

```bash
sudo apt install postgresql
sudo systemctl start postgresql
sudo -u postgres createdb myproject
echo "OPENPROSE_POSTGRES_URL=postgresql:///myproject" >> .prose/.env
```

--------------------------------

### OpenClaw config for inferrs (manual setup)

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/inferrs.md

This configuration example shows how to integrate inferrs as a custom provider in OpenClaw for a Gemma 4 model, assuming inferrs is started manually.

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      model: { primary: "inferrs/google/gemma-4-E2B-it" },
      models: {
        "inferrs/google/gemma-4-E2B-it": {
          alias: "Gemma 4 (inferrs)",
        },
      },
    },
  },
  models: {
    mode: "merge",
    providers: {
      inferrs: {
        baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",
        apiKey: "inferrs-local",
        api: "openai-completions",
        models: [
          {
            id: "google/gemma-4-E2B-it",
            name: "Gemma 4 E2B (inferrs)",
            reasoning: false,
            input: ["text"],
            cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
            contextWindow: 131072,
            maxTokens: 4096,
            compat: {
              requiresStringContent: true,
            },
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
}
```

### Create an Optional Channel Setup Surface

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/sdk-setup.md

Use this snippet to create an optional setup surface for a channel plugin, which generates both a setup adapter and a setup wizard for conditional installation contexts.

```typescript
import { createOptionalChannelSetupSurface } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-setup";

const setupSurface = createOptionalChannelSetupSurface({
  channel: "my-channel",
  label: "My Channel",
  npmSpec: "@myorg/openclaw-my-channel",
  docsPath: "/channels/my-channel",
});
// Returns { setupAdapter, setupWizard }
```

### Quick Start Deployment and Access

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/kubernetes.md

Sets up the necessary environment variables, deploys OpenClaw, and forwards the service port for local access. Ensure you replace <PROVIDER> with your actual model provider.

```bash
# Replace with your provider: ANTHROPIC, GEMINI, OPENAI, or OPENROUTER
export <PROVIDER>_API_KEY="..."
./scripts/k8s/deploy.sh

kubectl port-forward svc/openclaw 18789:18789 -n openclaw
open http://localhost:18789
```

### Example Project Environment File

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/scripts/clawdock/README.md

Template for <project>/.env containing Docker infrastructure variables (image name, ports, gateway token, config/workspace paths). Generated by setup.sh with a unique gateway token.

```bash
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw
OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw/workspace
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18789
OPENCLAW_BRIDGE_PORT=18790
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_BIND=lan
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<generated-by-docker-setup>
OPENCLAW_AUTH_PROFILE_SECRET_DIR=/Users/you/.openclaw-auth-profile-secrets
OPENCLAW_IMAGE=openclaw:local
```

--------------------------------

### Configuring setup Metadata in Plugin Manifest

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/manifest.md

This snippet illustrates the `setup` section, providing metadata for plugin setup and onboarding. It includes provider details, authentication methods, environment variables, CLI backends, and indicates if runtime hooks are required.

```json
{
  "setup": {
    "providers": [
      {
        "id": "openai",
        "authMethods": ["api-key"],
        "envVars": ["OPENAI_API_KEY"],
        "authEvidence": [
          {
            "type": "local-file-with-env",
            "fileEnvVar": "OPENAI_CREDENTIALS_FILE",
            "requiresAllEnv": ["OPENAI_PROJECT"],
            "credentialMarker": "openai-local-credentials",
            "source": "openai local credentials"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "cliBackends": ["openai-cli"],
    "configMigrations": ["legacy-openai-auth"],
    "requiresRuntime": false
  }
}
```

### Example SKILL.md with Frontmatter

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md

Complete example of a well-formed SKILL.md file showing required frontmatter fields (name, description) and basic workflow structure.

```markdown
---
name: pdf-tools
description: "Inspect, split, merge, OCR, redact, or convert PDFs with local CLI tools."
---

# PDF tools

Use for PDF manipulation. Prefer deterministic scripts for page edits.

## Workflow

1. Inspect file/page count.
2. Choose exact operation.
3. Write output beside input unless user asked otherwise.
4. Render/verify changed pages.
```

### Input/Output Bindings Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/open-prose/skills/prose/state/in-context.md

Demonstrates how inputs are received and outputs are defined within a program. Inputs are passed from the caller, and outputs are prepared to be returned to the caller.

```text
[Input] Inputs received:
   topic = "quantum computing" (from caller)
   depth = "deep" (from caller)

[Output] output findings = "Research shows..." (will return to caller)
[Output] output sources = ["arxiv:2401.1234", ...] (will return to caller)
```

--------------------------------

### Comprehensive CLI backend configuration example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/cli-backends.md

Illustrates a detailed configuration for a custom CLI backend, including command, arguments, output handling, session management, and image support.

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      cliBackends: {
        "my-cli": {
          command: "my-cli",
          args: ["--json"],
          output: "json",
          input: "arg",
          modelArg: "--model",
          modelAliases: {
            "claude-opus-4-6": "opus",
            "claude-sonnet-4-6": "sonnet",
          },
          sessionArg: "--session",
          sessionMode: "existing",
          sessionIdFields: ["session_id", "conversation_id"],
          systemPromptArg: "--system",
          // For CLIs with a dedicated prompt-file flag:
          // systemPromptFileArg: "--system-file",
          // Codex-style CLIs can point at a prompt file instead:
          // systemPromptFileConfigArg: "-c",
          // systemPromptFileConfigKey: "model_instructions_file",
          systemPromptWhen: "first",
          imageArg: "--image",
          imageMode: "repeat",
          // Opt in only if this backend may reseed safe invalidated sessions
          // from bounded raw OpenClaw transcript history before compaction.
          reseedFromRawTranscriptWhenUncompacted: true,
          serialize: true,
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### Setup CoreDNS for DNS-SD

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/dns.md

Use these commands to plan or apply the CoreDNS setup for unicast DNS-SD discovery. The `--apply` flag installs or updates the CoreDNS configuration and restarts the service, which requires sudo and is only supported on macOS.

```bash
openclaw dns setup
```

```bash
openclaw dns setup --domain openclaw.internal
```

```bash
openclaw dns setup --apply
```

--------------------------------

### Running OpenClaw Gateway in Foreground (WSL2)

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/help/faq.md

Command to start the OpenClaw Gateway in the foreground within WSL2 if the service was not installed.

```bash
openclaw gateway run
```
